questions.prompt: Why does the grower want notice of changes?

options.text: To plan the harvest
To avoid communicating with the restaurant
To make every delivery a week late

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 種植者需要時間計劃採收。

questions.prompt: Which arrangement do they favour?

options.text: Commit immediately to the largest possible order
Wait until the mushrooms spoil before ordering
Start with a modest order and review quantities together

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們建議先少量定期訂購，再根據實際用量調整。

script.speaker: Poppy
script.text: At the reunion they opened our school time capsule. My letter said I wanted to be a gardener, which surprised me.

script.speaker: Evan
script.text: You often say you had always planned to become a nurse. How old were you when you wrote it?

script.speaker: Poppy
script.text: Only eight. I remember enjoying the school garden, but I thought nursing had been my ambition even then.

script.speaker: Evan
script.text: Perhaps your later decision has become the beginning of the story you tell about yourself.

script.speaker: Poppy
script.text: The letter does not make that decision less important; it just shows there were other interests before it.

script.speaker: Evan
script.text: Exactly. You can keep the career story while giving your younger self more than one possible future.

questions.prompt: Why does the letter surprise Poppy?

options.text: It reveals an early ambition different from the one she usually recalls
It describes a career she has already retired from
It was written much later than she remembered

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 信中寫她想做園丁，與她一直說自己從小想做護士的記憶不同。

questions.prompt: What explanation does Evan suggest?

options.text: The school probably placed another pupil’s letter in the capsule
The letter proves she never enjoyed nursing
A later decision may have shaped her account of earlier years

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Evan 推測她後來的職業選擇可能影響了她對童年的敘述。

questions.prompt: How does Poppy interpret the new evidence?

options.text: It establishes that gardening was her only serious ambition
It adds an earlier interest without diminishing her later choice
It means her later choice was based on a false qualification

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Poppy 認為信件補充了早期興趣，並沒有削弱後來選擇護士的重要性。

script.speaker: Marta
script.text: I remember being sent to buy bread alone and feeling that the shop was very far from home.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: When we walked past it last year, it seemed only a few minutes away.

script.speaker: Marta
script.text: Perhaps the journey felt longer because I had never crossed that road without an adult.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: That sounds possible, though the route may have changed since then.

script.speaker: Marta
script.text: Either way, I still remember the pride of bringing the right loaf back.

script.speaker: Chris
script.text: The feeling can be real even when the exact distance or route is difficult to reconstruct.

questions.prompt: Why might the journey have seemed long to Marta?

options.text: The shop was certainly in another town
She had to carry several heavy bags
It was unfamiliar and she was travelling alone

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Marta 推測第一次獨自過馬路令路程感覺較長。

questions.prompt: What alternative does Chris mention?

options.text: The bread was probably delivered
The route might have changed
The shop may never have existed

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Chris 提出路線其後可能改變。

questions.prompt: What distinction does Chris make?

options.text: An emotion can be remembered even if practical details are uncertain
The journey must have been short in every year
Feelings are always more precise than maps

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 即使距離或路線未能確定，她記得的自豪感仍然可以是真實的。

script.speaker: Dawn
script.text: I found my grandmother’s sewing tin, and the smell reminded me of sitting beside her after school.

script.speaker: Yusuf
script.text: Do you remember learning to sew, or mainly watching her work?

script.speaker: Dawn
script.text: Mostly watching. I used to think I made the blue cushion, but my aunt says I only chose the buttons.

script.speaker: Yusuf
script.text: You could have helped in that smaller way and later remembered the whole project as yours.

script.speaker: Dawn
script.text: I like that explanation, though I cannot be certain without asking my grandmother.

script.speaker: Yusuf
script.text: The buttons still mattered to the finished cushion, even if someone else did the stitching.

questions.prompt: What triggered Dawn’s memory?

options.text: Receiving a letter from her grandmother
Finding the sewing tin and noticing its smell
Seeing a new cushion in a shop

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 縫紉盒的氣味令 Dawn 想起童年放學後陪伴祖母。

questions.prompt: What difference exists between Dawn’s memory and her aunt’s account?

options.text: Dawn recalls making the cushion; her aunt remembers her choosing buttons
Dawn remembers buttons; her aunt denies there was a cushion
Both agree Dawn completed every stitch alone

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Dawn 以為自己做了整個靠墊，姨媽則記得她只選了鈕扣。

questions.prompt: What does Yusuf suggest about the smaller contribution?

options.text: It proves the aunt’s memory is definitely correct
It has no connection to the cushion
It still played a part in the finished item

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Yusuf 指出即使只選鈕扣，也對完成品有貢獻。

script.speaker: Kofi
script.text: At my old school we played a game where the person who was caught chose the next activity.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: That differs from the version I knew, where the winner chose.

script.speaker: Kofi
script.text: I wonder whether our class changed the rule so that younger children could take part more easily.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: Possibly, but it could simply have been the version your teacher learned.

script.speaker: Kofi
script.text: I will ask a former classmate before writing that explanation in our reunion booklet.

script.speaker: Lily
script.text: Even then, call it a recollection unless someone finds a written rule from the time.

questions.prompt: How did Kofi’s version differ from Lily’s?

options.text: The caught player, rather than the winner, chose the next activity
Nobody was allowed to choose the next activity
Only teachers could take part in the game

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Kofi 的版本由被捉到的人選下一項活動，Lily 的版本則由勝出者選擇。

questions.prompt: Why does Lily suggest describing the explanation as a recollection?

options.text: Written rules never provide any evidence
The game was played at a different school last week
The reason for the rule is not yet established

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們尚未知道規則的真正來源，應把推測或回憶說清楚。

questions.prompt: What does Kofi intend to do before writing?

options.text: Remove every mention of the reunion
Ask a former classmate about the game
State his theory as a proven fact

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Kofi 打算先問舊同學，才寫入紀念冊。

script.speaker: Bea
script.text: My earliest holiday memory is a rough ferry crossing, though my parents remember a calm sea.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: Were you frightened of boats at the time? That might have made small movements feel dramatic.

script.speaker: Bea
script.text: I was, but my brother says the crossing was delayed by wind on another trip.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: Perhaps details from two journeys have become connected. Do your parents still have their travel dates?

script.speaker: Bea
script.text: They kept the tickets, so we might compare the dates with my brother’s photographs.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: It would be interesting to check, without assuming that any one person remembers the whole story perfectly.

questions.prompt: What might explain Bea’s vivid recollection of a rough crossing?

options.text: Her parents definitely travelled on a different ship
The ferry was cancelled before she boarded
Fear may have made ordinary movement feel more dramatic

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Malik 推測她當時怕船，小幅搖晃也可能令她感覺強烈。

questions.prompt: What evidence might help distinguish the trips?

options.text: A description of an unrelated holiday
Tickets and dated photographs
A new ferry timetable alone

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 船票日期與照片可能有助區分兩次旅程。

questions.prompt: What approach does Malik recommend?

options.text: Compare evidence while accepting that memories may be incomplete
Treat Bea’s memory as certainly false
Assume the delay proves both trips had rough seas

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Malik 建議比較證據，同時承認每個人的記憶都可能不完整。

script.text: We were there three years apart, so perhaps the music changed between us.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: Or one of us is combining it with a song from another occasion.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: The school archive has old programmes, though they may name the song without printing its lyrics.

The school’s music may have changed between their years there
The programmes show that both attended the same assembly

script.speaker: Ali
script.text: I want to post my neighbour’s soup recipe, but she showed it to me during a private visit.

script.speaker: Catherine
script.text: Even if the ingredients are ordinary, asking her first would respect the way she shared it.

script.speaker: Ali
script.text: She might be pleased, though she may not want her name or family story included.

script.speaker: Catherine
script.text: You could offer those choices separately, rather than treating permission to share as permission to name her.

script.speaker: Ali
script.text: I will show her the draft and ask whether she wants any changes before it goes online.

script.speaker: Catherine
script.text: That gives her a chance to decide what she is comfortable sharing.

questions.prompt: Why does Catherine recommend asking the neighbour?

options.text: The recipe was shared in a private setting
The neighbour has already agreed to publish the recipe under Ali’s name
The neighbour has already demanded publication

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 食譜是在私人探訪時分享，先徵求同意較尊重對方。

questions.prompt: What distinction does Catherine draw?

options.text: Acknowledging the neighbour would make asking her unnecessary
Removing the family story would automatically permit publication
Permission to share a recipe does not necessarily include permission to name its source

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 同意分享食譜不一定等於同意公開姓名或家族故事。

questions.prompt: What will Ali do before posting?

options.text: Ask readers to identify the neighbour
Show the draft to the neighbour and invite changes
Publish the family story without showing her

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ali 會先讓鄰居看草稿並詢問是否需要修改。

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Some people think a repair scheme should be universal. How would you respond?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: Before I answer, do you mean available to every household or free for every repair?

script.speaker: Host
script.text: I mean that every household could apply, although there might be a charge according to income.

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: In that case I support broad access, but I would want a simple application process.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: What concern lies behind that condition?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: If the form is difficult, people who most need help may be excluded even when they are formally eligible.

questions.prompt: Why does the candidate ask for clarification?

options.text: The host has refused to discuss repair schemes
The candidate has already decided all repairs must be free
The word universal could describe access or cost

questions.explanation_zh_hk: universal 可指人人有申請資格，也可指所有維修免費，候選人需要確認。

questions.prompt: What does the host mean by universal?

options.text: Only households above a fixed income may apply
Every household can apply, with possible income-related charges
Every repair is free for every household

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 主持人指所有住戶均可申請，但費用可能按收入而定。

questions.prompt: Why does the candidate favour a simple form?

options.text: Formal eligibility may be ineffective if applying is too difficult
A simple form guarantees every application will succeed
Income should never be considered in any scheme

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: You said online appointments always save time. What about someone whose connection fails during the call?

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: That is a fair counterexample. I should have said they can save travel time when the technology works.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: Would you therefore remove the online option entirely?

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: No. I would keep it alongside face-to-face appointments and make it easy to switch after a technical problem.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: Some services have limited staff. How would you decide what balance to offer?

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: I would look at demand and access needs, then review waiting times for both options.

questions.prompt: How does Elliot revise the original claim?

options.text: He says no appointments should be offered
He limits it to potential travel savings when technology works
He insists online appointments always save time

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Elliot 接受反例，將原先絕對的說法修正為科技正常時可能節省交通時間。

questions.prompt: What response does he propose after a connection failure?

options.text: Make switching to another appointment format straightforward
Remove all in-person appointments
Ask patients to repeat the same failed call indefinitely

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他建議保留兩種方式，並在技術故障後方便轉換。

questions.prompt: What information would guide the balance of appointments?

Only the preference of staff already working on online appointments
Demand, access needs and waiting times

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他會考慮需求、使用需要及兩種方式的輪候時間。

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: You suggested improving the town centre. What is one change you would make first?

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: How would you judge whether it had worked?

questions.prompt: Which change does the candidate identify?

Closing the town centre to pedestrians
Widening the waiting area at a crossing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 候選人建議擴闊過路處的等候空間。

questions.prompt: What would the proposed evaluation combine?

options.text: Feedback only from people who designed the new crossing
Observations of crowding and feedback from varied users
Only a prediction made before the work

Training for local volunteers
A guarantee of permanent volunteer availability

It has no possible benefits

The volunteers have already collected them

The organiser added a late-booking penalty

script.speaker: Toby

It says the attachment contains the final corrected timetable

Delete the booking page from the centre’s website
Draft a reminder without filling in the first date

The later date must be correct because it is on a website

The rehearsal can continue until ten as usual

The caretaker can decide whether the rehearsal needs to move again

script.text: One colleague also asked whether the card could be shared digitally because she works from another office.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: That makes sense, provided the colleague who is leaving is happy to receive everyone’s messages in a digital card.

script.speaker: Leila
script.text: I will offer both ways to contribute and keep the invitation brief.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: And make it clear that joining in is voluntary. A kind gesture loses something if people feel pressured.

questions.prompt: What would Martin say to colleagues with no personal story to share?

options.text: A brief good wish is enough if they choose to contribute
They should ask someone else for a memory to write as their own
They should sign only if they have worked closely with the recipient

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Martin 認為簡單祝福已足夠，毋須勉強寫個人回憶，而且參與應屬自願。

questions.prompt: Why does Martin qualify his support for a digital card?

options.text: He thinks messages from another office are less personal
He wants the recipient to approve every contribution in advance
He wants the recipient’s preference about the format checked

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Martin 願意用電子版本，但先要確認收卡的同事是否接受這種形式。

questions.prompt: What principle does Martin emphasise?

options.text: Remote colleagues should contribute only after the office card is complete
The gesture should allow voluntary participation without demanding intimacy
Every contribution should be equally personal to show equal respect

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Martin 強調自由參與，不應要求每個人都寫親密的個人內容。

title: The seating plan at a shared meal

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: For the community meal, I put the longest-serving members at the top table, as we usually do.

script.speaker: Dev
script.text: That recognises their contribution, but some newcomers may find it difficult to join a conversation if the established members are at a different table.

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: One founder has asked to sit beside the family she invited, rather than with the other committee members.

script.speaker: Dev
script.text: Could we ask for seating preferences and mix the tables, then thank the founders in the welcome speech?

script.speaker: Rosa
script.text: That would preserve the recognition without assuming a special table is what everyone wants.

script.speaker: Dev
script.text: Yes. We should check what the custom is meant to achieve before deciding which parts need to stay.

questions.prompt: What tension does Dev identify?

options.text: Mixing tables could prevent the founders from being thanked
The welcome speech may be too long for the invited families
Honouring longstanding members may make newcomers feel separate

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Dev 指出，特設主桌雖能表揚資深成員，卻可能令新參加者難以融入。

questions.prompt: What does the founder’s request show?

options.text: Invited families do not want to join mixed tables
A place of honour may not match an individual’s preference
The founders have agreed to sit away from the committee

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 創辦人想坐在自己邀請的家庭旁邊，顯示主桌安排未必符合每個人的意願。

questions.prompt: Which response best follows Dev’s final advice?

options.text: Let us keep the public thanks and ask people where they would feel comfortable sitting.
Let us keep the top table because recognition always requires separate seating.
Let us remove all mention of the founders so that every table is identical.

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Dev 建議先了解習俗的目的；保留致謝並詢問座位意願，能兼顧表揚與共融。

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: At the annual handover, the outgoing club chair normally presents a ceremonial key to the next chair.

script.speaker: Hiba
script.text: Will the new chair be able to attend? I heard she is caring for her father that evening.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: She cannot come, and one member thinks we should postpone the handover until she is free.

script.speaker: Hiba
script.text: Perhaps ask whether she would prefer a short video message and someone to accept the key on her behalf.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: I will offer that without asking her to explain her family situation to the whole club. The key is symbolic; the role starts on Monday either way.

script.speaker: Hiba
script.text: Then make the start date clear. The ceremony can adapt without delaying who is responsible for the club.

questions.prompt: Why does Owen distinguish the key from the role?

options.text: The outgoing chair will keep the role until both can attend
Changing the ceremony need not change when responsibility begins
The new chair needs the key to enter the club on Monday

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 鎖匙只具象徵意義；典禮可改動，但新主席仍會在星期一上任。

questions.prompt: What does Hiba suggest checking with the new chair?

options.text: Whether she would like a video message and someone to accept the key for her
Whether she can promise to attend after her role begins
Whether she wants her caring responsibilities announced

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hiba 建議詢問新主席是否願意錄製短片，並由別人代領鎖匙。

questions.prompt: What principle guides Hiba’s final comment?

options.text: Postpone official responsibilities whenever a ceremony is postponed
Keep the ceremony unchanged even if the new chair cannot take part
Preserve a clear transfer of responsibility while adapting the ritual

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hiba 認為儀式可以靈活調整，但必須清楚交代職責何時交接。

title: A visitor and a formal title

script.speaker: Anika
script.text: Our visitor introduced herself by her first name, but the programme gives her a professional title.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: In the formal introduction, using the title may be appropriate. Afterwards, we can follow the name she uses herself.

script.speaker: Anika
script.text: Should I assume everyone in her delegation prefers the same form of address?

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: I would not. If you are uncertain, ask each person how they would like to be addressed.

script.speaker: Anika
script.text: That seems better than treating a title as either mandatory or impolite in every setting.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: Yes. The relationship and occasion matter, and asking politely leaves room for individual preference.

questions.prompt: Why does Paul distinguish the formal introduction from later conversation?

options.text: The setting can affect which form of address is suitable
The visitor’s introduction makes her professional title invalid
The printed programme establishes a permanent rule for every conversation

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Paul 認為正式介紹與之後交談的場合不同，可採用不同稱呼。

questions.prompt: Which response best applies Paul’s advice to the other delegates?

options.text: I will use first names for everyone because the visitor introduced herself that way.
I will use each printed title even if a delegate requests a different name.
I will ask anyone whose preference is unclear rather than copy the visitor’s choice.

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Paul 建議不確定時逐一詢問，不應假設整個代表團都偏好同一稱呼。

questions.prompt: What is Paul’s overall view of titles?

options.text: A professional title should take priority over a person’s stated preference
Their appropriateness depends on context and individual preference
A first-name introduction makes titles impolite in formal settings

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Paul 認為應考慮場合、關係及個人意願，沒有適用於所有情況的硬性規則。

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: We usually decorate a desk on a colleague’s birthday, but our new teammate has said she dislikes surprises.

script.speaker: Miles
script.text: Perhaps ask whether she would enjoy a quiet card or would rather not mark the day at work at all.

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: I do not want the rest of the team to think she is rejecting their kindness.

script.speaker: Miles
script.text: You can explain that people celebrate differently without sharing anything she wants kept private.

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: If she prefers no celebration, we can still welcome her in ways she has actually chosen.

script.speaker: Miles
script.text: Exactly. A custom works best when it makes the person concerned feel comfortable, rather than obliged.

questions.prompt: What assumption about the desk decoration is being questioned?

options.text: That the team has permission to move the colleague’s work
That the colleague would prefer a larger celebration outside work
That the team’s usual gesture will make this colleague feel welcome

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 新同事已說不喜歡驚喜，因此不能假設慣常的佈置會令她感到受歡迎。

questions.prompt: Which two options does Miles suggest checking?

options.text: A private party or organising the next team birthday
A quiet card or no workplace celebration
A surprise at her desk or a surprise outside work

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Miles 建議問她想要簡單送卡，還是不在工作場合慶祝。

questions.prompt: How does Miles suggest explaining the choice to the team?

options.text: Acknowledge different preferences while protecting private information
Explain her personal reasons so the team will accept the decision
Describe the usual custom as inappropriate for every future birthday

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Miles 建議只說大家慶祝方式不同，毋須透露她希望保密的事情。

script.speaker: Gareth
script.text: The programme includes a minute of silence, but a parent asked what her young child should do during it.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: We could explain its purpose in advance and say that families are welcome to step outside if needed.

script.speaker: Gareth
script.text: Would leaving the room be seen as disrespectful by other guests?

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Not if the announcement makes clear that people have different needs and that a quiet exit is welcome.

script.speaker: Gareth
script.text: I will also show the timing on the printed programme, so families can prepare without drawing attention.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: That preserves the moment while making it easier for more people to take part in a way that suits them.

questions.prompt: Why show the timing in the printed programme?

options.text: Parents can explain their needs publicly before choosing where to sit
Families can plan discreetly rather than seek an exception during the silence
Families can decide the length of the silence once the event begins

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 列明時間可讓家庭預先準備，毋須在儀式期間引起注意或解釋需要。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the proposed announcement?

options.text: To establish that leaving quietly can be a respectful response to different needs
To advise all families with children to leave before the silence
To ask departing guests to explain why they cannot remain

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 公告會清楚說明不同人有不同需要，安靜離場亦可接受。

questions.prompt: What balance do they seek?

options.text: Keep everyone in the room by shortening the silence for all
Leave participation rules unstated so nobody feels singled out
Retain the shared moment while allowing flexible participation

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們希望保留默哀的意義，同時讓不同家庭按需要參與。

script.speaker: Tess
script.text: I heard a phrase at my friend’s family gathering and thought of using it in my speech because it sounded cheerful.

script.speaker: Hamid
script.text: Do you know what it means and when the family normally uses it? The sound alone may not tell you that.

script.speaker: Tess
script.text: No, and I would not want to use it in a way that makes someone’s tradition into a joke.

script.speaker: Hamid
script.text: You could ask your friend to explain it and whether it would be appropriate in this particular speech.

script.speaker: Tess
script.text: If she is unsure, I can choose my own words rather than put her in the position of speaking for everyone.

script.speaker: Hamid
script.text: That sounds respectful. Curiosity is welcome, and so is accepting that a phrase may not fit every occasion.

questions.prompt: What concern underlies Hamid’s first question?

options.text: A cheerful sound does not establish the phrase’s meaning or appropriate use
A phrase heard at a gathering is unlikely to be suitable for any speech
The family may expect Tess to translate her whole speech

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hamid 提醒她，聽起來歡快並不代表已了解詞語的意思和使用場合。

questions.prompt: Why would Tess avoid pressing her friend for a definite answer?

options.text: She thinks her friend is unwilling to explain the phrase’s meaning
She has already decided to use the phrase regardless of context
She does not expect one person to speak for a whole tradition

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Tess 不想令朋友承擔代表所有人作決定的壓力；不肯定時可用自己的說法。

questions.prompt: What attitude does Hamid endorse?

options.text: Avoid asking about unfamiliar language because curiosity is disrespectful
Learn about the context and accept that the phrase may not fit
Use the phrase if it sounds positive, with an explanation afterwards

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hamid 鼓勵了解背景，同時接受某句話未必適用於這個場合。

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: The proposed crossing is near the shops, but the dropped kerb is several metres away from the marked route.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: That could force wheelchair users into the road at an awkward angle. Has anyone tested the design on site?

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: The drawing was displayed at the consultation, although I did not see a trial with people who use mobility aids.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: We should ask for one before the layout is finalised, and include people pushing prams as well.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: I support the crossing in principle; I just want the approach to be as usable as the crossing itself.

script.speaker: Raj
script.text: Then say both in your response. Identifying a practical problem need not mean opposing the whole scheme.

questions.prompt: Why might the drawing alone be insufficient?

options.text: It omits the location of the shops beside the crossing
It establishes that the dropped kerb cannot be moved
It has not shown how people with mobility needs would negotiate the approach

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 圖則雖已公開展示，但未見有行動需要的人實地試用，通道是否方便仍需驗證。

questions.prompt: What do they propose before the layout is finalised?

options.text: A decision based on whether the marked route looks straight on paper
An on-site trial involving mobility-aid users and people with prams
A new consultation limited to people who already support the drawing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們建議由使用行動輔助工具及推嬰兒車的人實地測試。

questions.prompt: What is Helen’s position?

options.text: She supports a crossing but wants a practical flaw corrected
She will oppose the crossing unless all other street changes stop
She thinks the kerb matters less than getting any crossing approved

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Helen 原則上支持設立過路處，但希望解決通往過路處的實際問題。

script.speaker: Tara
script.text: The last bus arrives at the station five minutes after the train leaves, so my journey home takes an extra hour.

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: Is that every evening, or only when the bus is delayed?

script.speaker: Tara
script.text: It is in the published timetable. I have checked for three weekdays, although weekend services are different.

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: Then send the operator the specific connection and dates. Other passengers could add their experiences too.

script.speaker: Tara
script.text: I will ask whether the bus can leave earlier, but I realise that might affect people boarding at previous stops.

script.speaker: Elliot
script.text: A useful response could consider the whole route. The operator may have another way to improve the connection.

questions.prompt: Why does Elliot ask whether the problem occurs only when the bus is delayed?

options.text: He wants to show that the train is usually responsible for delays
He wants to distinguish a timetable mismatch from unreliable running
He suspects Tara has confused weekday and weekend services

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Elliot 先分清是班次本身銜接不良，還是巴士延誤造成錯過火車。

questions.prompt: Why does Tara qualify her request for an earlier bus?

options.text: The change could disadvantage passengers using earlier stops
An earlier bus would require changing the weekend train timetable
She has not yet checked whether the published connection exists

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Tara 明白提早開車可能影響較早各站的乘客，因此沒有假設只需直接改時間。

questions.prompt: What would best support a useful request to the operator?

options.text: An assumption that the weekend connection has the same problem
A demand for the same departure time on every route
The affected weekday services, dates and experiences of other passengers

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 具體班次、日期及其他乘客經驗可幫助營辦商評估整條路線。

title: A community notice in two places

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: The council is moving notices online, but some residents still look for them in the window of the village shop.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: Could the shop display a short printed summary with a number to call for the full information?

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: The owner is willing, although she cannot promise to replace notices every time a date changes.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: Then the council needs to assign someone to check the display and remove outdated copies.

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: We should also make sure the phone number reaches a person who can answer questions, not just a recording.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: Agreed. Two channels are useful only if both remain accurate and accessible.

questions.prompt: What does Colin’s proposal aim to preserve?

options.text: Access for people who still use the shop display
The shop owner’s control over council announcements
A printed version containing every detail of the online notice

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 簡短紙本摘要及查詢電話可讓仍依靠村店告示的居民取得資訊。

questions.prompt: Why must responsibility for the display be assigned?

options.text: The owner has refused to display notices unless she writes them
The council has decided that print and online dates should differ
The owner cannot reliably replace copies whenever information changes

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 店主不能保證每次日期更改都更新，所以議會須安排專人檢查及移除舊告示。

questions.prompt: What is the shared view of using two channels?

options.text: It is worthwhile only if every resident uses both methods
It helps only if both are maintained and lead to usable information
It guarantees access as soon as an online link is printed

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們認為兩種渠道都必須保持準確，並讓居民得到實際有用的資訊與協助。

title: The empty flat above the café

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: The owner wants to turn the empty flat above the café into a holiday let instead of renting it to a local tenant.

script.speaker: Kamal
script.text: Visitors may support the café, but one less long-term home matters in a village where rentals are scarce.

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: The owner says seasonal income would help pay for repairs the building urgently needs.

script.speaker: Kamal
script.text: That is relevant too. Can the council tell us what rules apply and whether any repair grants are available?

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: I will ask before assuming the owner has an easy alternative. We also need evidence about local housing demand.

script.speaker: Kamal
script.text: Yes. A useful discussion should consider the building’s condition as well as who needs somewhere to live.

questions.prompt: Which competing considerations shape their discussion?

options.text: The café’s opening hours and the tenant’s preferred holiday dates
The number of café tables and the cost of the visitors’ transport
Repair income for the building and scarce long-term rental housing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 假日出租可能帶來維修收入，但也會減少本已短缺的長期出租單位。

questions.prompt: Why ask about repair grants?

options.text: The owner has agreed to accept any grant instead of holiday income
Support might change the owner’s options for financing the work
A grant would establish that there is no local housing demand

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 維修資助可能增加業主的選擇，因此應先查詢，再評估是否有可行替代方案。

questions.prompt: What approach does Ruth adopt?

options.text: Check the options and evidence before assuming there is a simple solution
Accept the holiday let because repairs outweigh housing needs
Reject the holiday let without considering the building’s condition

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ruth 不先假設問題容易解決，而是查詢規則、資助及房屋需求。

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: During the school street trial, cars cannot enter the road at drop-off time, but deliveries have been arriving then for years.

script.speaker: Rob
script.text: The cleaner air may help children, while the shop still needs a practical way to receive stock.

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: The owner says an earlier delivery might work on some days, though her supplier serves several villages.

script.speaker: Rob
script.text: Could the trial record delivery problems as well as traffic levels and ask the supplier about its schedule?

script.speaker: Nadia
script.text: That would give the review something more useful than counting complaints on either side.

script.speaker: Rob
script.text: Exactly. The trial should show what can be adjusted, not just whether people initially approve.

questions.prompt: What practical conflict does the trial expose?

options.text: Parents are being asked to deliver stock during the school run
The restricted period overlaps with established shop deliveries
The supplier’s route is being moved away from all the villages

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 試行禁車的時間與店舖多年來的送貨時間重疊。

questions.prompt: Why collect delivery problems alongside traffic levels?

options.text: The review should identify workable adjustments as well as benefits
Traffic levels matter only if the shop makes no complaints
A count of complaints would prove which side deserves priority

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 同時收集送貨問題與交通資料，才能了解試行的效果及可調整之處。

questions.prompt: What does Rob think a trial should achieve?

options.text: Establish whether the supplier will accept the original scheme unchanged
Allow the shop’s existing schedule to determine every traffic restriction
Reveal what can be adapted rather than simply measure initial approval

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Rob 認為試行應找出可改善之處，不能只統計最初有多少人贊成。

script.speaker: Ivy
script.text: The market square has plenty of space, but my father cannot shop for long because there is nowhere to sit.

script.speaker: Mo
script.text: A bench near the entrance might help, although it should not block the route for deliveries or wheelchairs.

script.speaker: Ivy
script.text: The traders suggested using the area beside the planter, but it is exposed to rain.

script.speaker: Mo
script.text: Could we ask older shoppers and mobility groups where seating would be most useful before choosing a site?

script.speaker: Ivy
script.text: We could also check who would maintain a shelter if the council agrees to one.

script.speaker: Mo
script.text: Good point. A seat is a simple idea, but its location and upkeep determine whether people can use it.

questions.prompt: Why might the traders’ suggested location be inadequate?

options.text: It offers space for a seat but little protection from rain
It blocks the entrance already used for wheelchair access
It is too far from the planter to allow a shelter

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 花槽旁雖可放座位，但位置沒有遮雨設施，仍要考慮遮蔽。

questions.prompt: Why consult older shoppers and mobility groups?

options.text: Their agreement would remove the need to consider delivery access
They have already offered to fund and maintain the shelter
Their experience can help identify where seating would actually be useful

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 使用者的實際經驗可幫助選擇有用的位置，但不能代替通道及保養規劃。

questions.prompt: What does Mo’s final comment stress?

options.text: A council decision on a shelter would settle every maintenance question
Providing an object is only useful if its placement and upkeep work
The bench should be installed first and its location reviewed later

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mo 指出，座位的選址及保養會決定它是否真正實用。

script.speaker: Pete
script.text: The library plans a reading room upstairs, but the listed building has no lift and the stairs are steep.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: It would be disappointing to call the project inclusive if some residents cannot reach the room.

script.speaker: Pete
script.text: The manager says structural changes need approval, so a lift might take longer than the refurbishment.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: Could an equivalent room downstairs be offered in the meantime, with the same books and activities?

script.speaker: Pete
script.text: I will suggest that, while asking for a clear timetable for a longer-term accessible solution.

script.speaker: Sana
script.text: That addresses the immediate barrier without treating a temporary arrangement as the end of the work.

questions.prompt: What is Sana’s concern about describing the project as inclusive?

options.text: The downstairs room would offer a wider selection of books
The refurbishment timetable has already ruled out all access changes
Some residents could not reach the proposed reading room

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 沒有升降機且樓梯陡峭，部分居民無法上樓，因此稱項目共融並不恰當。

questions.prompt: What would make the temporary downstairs room equivalent?

options.text: Use only by people who have already booked the upstairs room
Access to the same books and activities
A similar name but fewer activities until the lift is approved

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Sana 建議樓下房間提供相同書籍及活動，並非較次等的替代安排。

questions.prompt: Why does Pete also want a timetable?

options.text: Immediate access should not remove pressure for a lasting solution
The temporary room needs to close before structural approval is requested
The manager has promised to finish the lift before the refurbishment

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Pete 希望臨時措施與長遠改善並行，避免臨時安排成為工作的終點。

script.speaker: Eve
script.text: The orchard invites families to press surplus apples, but last year some fruit went unused after the event.

script.speaker: Kieran
script.text: Could a nearby kitchen take the remainder, provided the fruit is sound and someone can transport it promptly?

script.speaker: Eve
script.text: The kitchen manager is interested, though she needs an estimate before arranging volunteers and storage.

script.speaker: Kieran
script.text: We could give her a rough range now, then weigh what remains at midday and phone her before anyone comes to collect it.

script.speaker: Eve
script.text: I will check the handling requirements too. Fruit intended for food needs more care than fruit for compost.

script.speaker: Kieran
script.text: Then tell participants where each container goes, so enthusiasm does not create extra sorting afterwards.

questions.prompt: Why is an estimate important to the kitchen?

options.text: The estimate determines whether any fruit can be composted
The amount affects how it organises volunteers and storage
The kitchen needs to set the orchard’s pressing schedule

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 廚房需要知道大約數量，才能安排義工及儲存空間。

questions.prompt: What condition limits the offer to donate the remaining apples?

options.text: They must be suitable for food and transported promptly
They must all have been picked during the event itself
They must be weighed before any family presses apples

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Kieran 提出水果要完好適合食用，而且能及時運送，才可交給廚房。

questions.prompt: What problem could clear container instructions prevent?

options.text: The kitchen having to confirm the quantity after the event
Volunteers needing any information about safe food handling
Extra sorting caused by mixing food donations with compost material

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 標清食用捐贈與堆肥容器，可避免參加者混放水果，事後要額外分類。

script.speaker: Mara
script.text: The café wants fifty handmade mugs in exactly the same shade as the sample, but my glaze varies slightly in the kiln.

script.speaker: Glyn
script.text: Could you show them several finished pieces so they understand the range before placing an order?

script.speaker: Mara
script.text: Yes, and I will explain that slight variation is part of the process, so I cannot guarantee an exact match.

script.speaker: Glyn
script.text: They may still need a fairly consistent appearance for their shelves. Ask what range they would accept.

script.speaker: Mara
script.text: If they need an exact colour, I would rather say now that I cannot guarantee it than disappoint them after taking the order.

script.speaker: Glyn
script.text: That gives them a genuine choice and protects the relationship if the finished batch looks different.

questions.prompt: What does showing several finished pieces establish?

options.text: The range of colour variation the buyer should expect
Which single sample every mug will exactly reproduce
That the café has agreed to accept any shade produced

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 多件成品可展示正常色差範圍，但仍須詢問客人能否接受。

questions.prompt: What should Mara establish before accepting the order?

options.text: Which glaze sample the café wants her to guarantee exactly
Whether the café regards any variation as proof of damage
How much variation the café can accept

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 她應先確認咖啡店可接受多少色差，才決定能否接單。

questions.prompt: Why would Mara decline an exact-colour requirement?

options.text: She expects the café to change its display regardless of the mugs’ colour
She values an honest agreement over a promise she cannot reliably meet
She thinks handmade work should be exempt from discussing expectations

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mara 寧願事先坦言做不到完全同色，也不想承諾無法穩定達到的要求。

script.speaker: Ellis
script.text: Our small mill could deliver flour to two more bakeries, but the van is already nearly full on Fridays.

script.speaker: Jude
script.text: Could one bakery receive its order on Thursday, when the van returns from the northern route half empty?

script.speaker: Ellis
script.text: Possibly, although the baker would need dry storage for an extra day. I should ask rather than assume.

script.speaker: Jude
script.text: Also compare the extra mileage with the benefit of combining journeys. A fuller van is not automatically the shortest route.

script.speaker: Ellis
script.text: I will map both options and include the driver’s working hours before quoting a delivery price.

script.speaker: Jude
script.text: That should give the baker a practical choice and prevent the round from becoming unrealistic for the driver.

questions.prompt: What makes Thursday worth investigating?

options.text: It would avoid the need for the baker to store flour
The new bakeries have already rejected Friday deliveries
There is unused capacity on a route already being operated

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 周四現有路線回程有空間，因此值得研究，但仍需確認路線及儲存安排。

questions.prompt: Why must the baker be consulted?

options.text: The baker would have to take over the northern delivery route
An earlier delivery would require an extra day of dry storage
The van’s spare capacity means the baker must take a larger order

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 提早一天收貨需要多一天的乾燥儲存空間，不能假設麵包店一定有。

questions.prompt: What does Jude caution against assuming?

options.text: That a fuller vehicle necessarily produces a more efficient route
That driver hours can be included when quoting the price
That two routes can be compared before the baker agrees

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jude 提醒，載貨較滿不代表路程較短；仍須比較里數及工作時間。

script.speaker: Sian
script.text: A customer returned a basket with a broken handle and asked whether I could make it look completely new.

script.speaker: Harvey
script.text: Can you replace just the damaged weave without weakening the rest of the basket?

script.speaker: Sian
script.text: Probably, but the fresh willow will be lighter until it ages. I cannot promise an invisible repair.

script.speaker: Harvey
script.text: Show the customer a repaired example and explain the colour change before agreeing a price.

script.speaker: Sian
script.text: I will also check whether the basket carries heavy shopping, because that affects how I reinforce the handle.

script.speaker: Harvey
script.text: That is sensible. The appearance and the intended use both matter when deciding how to repair it.

questions.prompt: Why can Sian not promise an invisible repair?

options.text: The customer’s use of the basket has already changed its shape
Fresh willow will initially be lighter than the older material
The handle has to be reinforced with a different painted material

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 新柳條起初會比舊物料淺色，要待時間過去才逐漸變色。

questions.prompt: Why does intended use affect the repair?

options.text: The expected load influences how much reinforcement the handle needs
Heavy shopping would guarantee that the repaired colour matches sooner
A basket used for shopping cannot have its handle repaired

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 若籃子要承載重物，手柄便可能需要較強加固。

questions.prompt: Which response would best continue Harvey’s advice?

options.text: I will quote for an invisible repair first and discuss the fresh willow after the work is done.
I will reinforce it in the same way whatever the customer intends to carry.
I will show how the colour will differ and ask what the basket normally carries before quoting.

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 先展示色差並了解用途，才能讓客人知情決定合適的修補方法及價錢。

script.speaker: June
script.text: The jam label says strawberries from our farm, but the last batch also used fruit from a neighbouring county when our crop failed.

script.speaker: Arun
script.text: Then the wording should make the source clear instead of letting customers assume every berry came from this farm.

script.speaker: June
script.text: We could name both farms on the label, although the proportions change with each batch.

script.speaker: Arun
script.text: That sounds honest if both actually supplied that batch. Keep a record so the label can be checked.

script.speaker: June
script.text: I will print smaller batches of labels, even though that takes more time than using the same roll all season.

script.speaker: Arun
script.text: It may take longer, but customers can then understand what they are buying without guessing.

questions.prompt: What problem does Arun identify with the existing wording?

options.text: The label claims a farm origin that does not apply to all the fruit
The label identifies both farms but gives the wrong proportions
Customers may think the jam is made entirely outside the region

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 原有字眼可能令人以為全部水果來自這個農場；實際上部分來自另一供應農場。

questions.prompt: When would naming both farms be accurate?

options.text: Whenever either farm has supplied the shop at some point in the season
Only when the two farms supply exactly equal quantities
When both supplied fruit for the particular batch being labelled

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Arun 說只有兩個農場確實供應了該批水果，才可在那一批的標籤列出兩者。

questions.prompt: Why is printing smaller batches worth the extra work?

options.text: Smaller labels will show the proportion of fruit without checking it
Labels can follow changing sources instead of outlasting their accuracy
The shop can avoid keeping records once a new label is printed

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 少量印製可按每批來源更新，避免整季沿用已不準確的標籤。

script.speaker: Alma
script.text: A visitor asked me to alter her coat while she waited at the craft fair, but I would need to inspect the lining first.

script.speaker: Benji
script.text: Could you offer an assessment today and arrange the work later if the lining makes it more complicated?

script.speaker: Alma
script.text: Yes. I can give a range of prices, but I should not give a final quote until I know what the job involves.

script.speaker: Benji
script.text: Make clear whether the assessment costs anything, and when she can expect your findings and final quote.

script.speaker: Alma
script.text: I will write that down for her and explain that the collection date will be confirmed once I have checked the coat and she accepts the quote.

script.speaker: Benji
script.text: That should prevent either of you from mistaking an estimate for a confirmed agreement.

questions.prompt: Why does Alma prefer an assessment before a final quote?

options.text: The visitor has already agreed to pay for any additional work
Assessing the coat would commit the visitor to having it altered
The lining may reveal work not apparent from the outside

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 內襯可能令修改更複雜，因此要先檢查，才能確定工作範圍及報價。

questions.prompt: What does Benji want made explicit before the visitor decides?

options.text: A collection date that applies even if the visitor declines the work
Any assessment fee and when the assessment will be completed
A final alteration price before the lining has been inspected

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Benji 要求清楚說明評估是否收費，以及何時會有評估結果。

questions.prompt: What misunderstanding are they trying to prevent?

options.text: Treating a provisional estimate as a settled agreement
Treating a final quote as permission to inspect the lining
Assuming the visitor wants the coat returned after the fair

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們要避免把暫估價誤當成已確認的協議。

script.speaker: Molly
script.text: The restaurant asked whether I could grow a lemon-scented basil for its summer menu, but it has not decided how much it would buy.

script.speaker: Rafi
script.text: Would a small trial plot let the chef test it before you give up land used for reliable crops?

script.speaker: Molly
script.text: Yes, though the chef wants enough for several tasting sessions. I need to know when those would be.

script.speaker: Rafi
script.text: Agree the trial quantity and dates first, and distinguish that order from any possible regular supply.

script.speaker: Molly
script.text: If the trial goes well, I can discuss next season, but planting a whole field now would leave me carrying all the risk.

script.speaker: Rafi
script.text: Exactly. Interest in a new product is useful, but it is not the same as a commitment to buy it.

questions.prompt: Why does Rafi suggest a small trial plot?

options.text: It avoids having to agree dates for the tasting sessions
It allows testing while limiting the grower’s exposure to uncertain demand
It guarantees the restaurant will order the whole crop

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 小規模試種可讓廚師試用，同時減低需求未明對種植者造成的風險。

questions.prompt: What should be agreed before the trial begins?

options.text: A specific quantity and tasting schedule, separate from future supply
A full field of basil for an unspecified number of meals
A regular order that starts before the chef tastes the herb

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 試種前應確認數量及試食時間，並與日後可能的常規供貨分開處理。

questions.prompt: What distinction does Rafi make?

options.text: A successful trial always requires a full field of the crop
A tasting order prevents any discussion of future supply
Expressing interest does not amount to agreeing a purchase

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Rafi 指出，表示有興趣不等於已承諾購買。

script.speaker: Clare
script.text: When I was ten, I lost my return train ticket on a trip with my grandfather and was sure we would be stranded.

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: Did he find it before the train arrived, or did you have to miss the train?

script.speaker: Clare
script.text: Neither. He calmly explained the situation at the ticket office and bought another ticket in time, although I knew money was tight.

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: I imagine you felt guilty as well as relieved. Did he mention the cost afterwards?

script.speaker: Clare
script.text: Only once, to suggest keeping important things in a zipped pocket. Years later I understood how deliberately calm he had been.

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: The memory seems to have changed as you grew older: first it was about the ticket, then about his kindness.

questions.prompt: How was the immediate problem resolved?

options.text: Her grandfather paid for a replacement ticket
The ticket office found the original ticket
They postponed the journey until the ticket was found

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 祖父到售票處說明情況，並買了另一張車票。

questions.prompt: What did Clare come to appreciate as she grew older?

options.text: He had known the ticket would be found before they travelled
The replacement had cost less than she had originally imagined
His calm response had required effort because the expense mattered

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Clare 長大後才明白，祖父在手頭拮据下仍刻意保持冷靜，是一份體諒。

questions.prompt: How does Daniel interpret the changing meaning of the memory?

options.text: Clare now sees the pocket advice as more important than the calm response
Clare now notices her grandfather’s kindness behind the practical solution
Clare has replaced an accurate childhood memory with a different event

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Daniel 認為她兒時只在意車票，長大後才看懂祖父處理事情時的善意。

script.speaker: Grace
script.text: The community centre is considering a tool library, so residents can borrow a drill instead of each buying one.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: That might reduce purchases, but someone would need to inspect the tools and explain how to use them safely.

script.speaker: Grace
script.text: A local repairer has offered to train volunteers, although we have not yet found money for replacement parts.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: Could you start with a small selection and keep a record of repairs, borrowing and costs?

script.speaker: Grace
script.text: Yes. We can then decide whether demand justifies expanding, rather than collecting equipment we cannot maintain.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: And publish the borrowing conditions clearly, including what happens if a tool is damaged or returned late.

questions.prompt: What qualifies Hassan’s support for the idea?

options.text: Avoiding purchases matters more than whether the tools can be maintained
Volunteer training would remove the need for any future inspections
Sharing tools still requires safety checks and clear borrowing conditions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hassan 認為共用工具有好處，但仍需檢查、使用指導及清楚的借用條款。

questions.prompt: What remains unresolved despite the repairer’s offer?

options.text: Whether the centre is considering shared tools
How replacement parts will be funded
Whether anyone can provide volunteer training

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 維修師傅願意培訓義工，但替換零件的資金仍未解決。

questions.prompt: Why keep records during a small initial scheme?

options.text: To judge whether demand and maintenance costs support expansion
To establish that trained volunteers will never need spare parts
To delay publishing conditions until enough people have borrowed tools

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 先記錄借用量、維修及成本，可按實際需求和維持能力決定是否擴展。

script.speaker: Jo
script.text: The arts centre wants to charge for its workshop because the materials and tutor are expensive.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: A fee could keep the programme running, but it might exclude people who would benefit most.

script.speaker: Jo
script.text: What if participants could pay what they can, with a suggested amount that reflects the actual cost?

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: That could help, although the centre would need enough income to cover the difference. Perhaps a sponsor could fund some places.

script.speaker: Jo
script.text: I would also ask privately about anything that might prevent people taking part, rather than making anyone explain their finances at the door.

script.speaker: Malik
script.text: Agreed. Fair access and a sustainable budget both need attention, and neither happens automatically.

questions.prompt: What tension does Malik identify?

options.text: Materials are expensive only when the workshop is fully booked
Covering the programme’s costs may make access harder for some people
A suggested contribution would necessarily cost more than a fixed fee

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Malik 指出，收費可維持活動，但也可能令最有需要的人無法參加。

questions.prompt: Why might sponsorship still be needed under a pay-what-you-can arrangement?

options.text: Participants’ contributions may fall short of the cost
Every participant would be required to pay the suggested amount
The suggested amount would exclude materials from the budget

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 自定付款額未必足以支付全部成本，因此可能需要贊助補貼部分名額。

questions.prompt: What concern guides Jo’s suggestion about asking privately?

options.text: People should explain their finances before asking about access needs
Private conversations would remove the need to plan a sustainable budget
People should be able to discuss access without public financial disclosure

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jo 希望私下了解參與需要，避免有人要在門口公開交代財務狀況。

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: You have said that digital services will make every high street unnecessary. Do you think there are any exceptions?

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: Yes. I stated that too strongly. Some people value seeing products in person, and others need services they can reach without using an app.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: How would you revise your prediction to take those needs into account?

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: I would say online services may reduce demand for some shops, while high streets could adapt by offering a mixture of services and social spaces.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: Does that mean every town will adapt successfully?

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: No. The result will depend on local resources and transport, so I would avoid promising the same outcome everywhere.

questions.prompt: What prompts Maya to revise her original claim?

options.text: She recognises needs that digital services alone may not meet
The examiner supplies evidence that all online services are declining
She realises that every high street already offers the same services

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Maya 承認有些人需要親身看商品或不用程式便可使用的服務，所以原說法太絕對。

questions.prompt: How does her revised prediction differ from the first?

options.text: It predicts that every town will replace shops with identical social spaces
It assumes online demand will disappear once shops offer more services
It allows different roles for high streets rather than assuming they will all become unnecessary

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 修改後的預測容許商業街透過不同服務轉型，不再斷言所有商業街都會失去作用。

questions.prompt: Which follow-up answer is most consistent with her final position?

options.text: I would use the number of apps alone to decide whether a town can adapt.
I would compare local resources and transport before predicting how a particular town will adapt.
I would expect the same outcome wherever a town introduces digital services.

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Maya 說結果取決於本地資源及交通，因此要了解個別城鎮的條件才作預測。

script.speaker: Rhea
script.text: I wanted to challenge the lecturer’s conclusion, but the questions afterwards seemed to be about definitions.

script.speaker: Callum
script.text: You could still ask how her conclusion accounts for the evidence that appeared to contradict it.

script.speaker: Rhea
script.text: Would that sound as though I was accusing her of ignoring the evidence?

script.speaker: Callum
script.text: Not if you explain what you understood first and invite her to clarify the connection.

script.speaker: Rhea
script.text: Then I might discover that I misunderstood the graph rather than the argument itself.

script.speaker: Callum
script.text: Exactly. A respectful challenge can improve your understanding even when you end up changing your own view.

questions.prompt: What concerns Rhea about her question?

options.text: It might reveal that she missed the whole lecture
It might repeat a definition the lecturer has already explained
It might sound like an accusation

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Rhea 擔心問題聽起來像指責講者忽略證據。

questions.prompt: What does Callum recommend she do first?

options.text: Wait for another student to ask the same question
Explain her understanding before asking for clarification
State that the conclusion is wrong before discussing the graph

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Callum 建議先說明自己的理解，再請講者澄清。

questions.prompt: What benefit does Callum see in a challenge?

options.text: It may deepen understanding even if the questioner changes their mind
It allows the questioner to defend their first interpretation without revising it
It is useful only if the lecturer withdraws the conclusion

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 即使最後改變自己看法，提出質疑仍可加深理解。

script.speaker: Amina
script.text: The college is offering a study app that promises to identify the topics we are weakest at.

script.speaker: Rob
script.text: That sounds useful, but does it explain how it reaches that judgement?

script.speaker: Amina
script.text: It counts mistakes in short quizzes. I suppose a rushed answer could look like a gap in knowledge.

script.speaker: Rob
script.text: Yes, and a correct guess could hide one. I would use its suggestions as a starting point.

script.speaker: Amina
script.text: We could compare them with our coursework feedback before deciding what to revise.

script.speaker: Rob
script.text: And tell the college what happens after a trial, especially if the app repeatedly misidentifies a topic.

questions.prompt: Why might the app misjudge a student?

options.text: It treats unanswered questions as correct answers
Quiz answers can reflect haste or guessing
It judges revision needs from coursework rather than quiz results

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 趕答或猜中答案都可能令小測結果未能反映真正理解。

questions.prompt: How do they plan to use its suggestions?

options.text: Compare them with feedback from coursework
Use them to replace feedback from their tutors
Recommend the app before comparing its results

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們會把程式建議與課業評語比較。

questions.prompt: What is Rob’s attitude to the app?

options.text: Convinced that the app is more reliable than coursework feedback
Unwilling to test it until it can explain every incorrect answer
Cautiously interested, with a wish to evaluate its results

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Rob 覺得建議可作起點，但希望試用後評估準確度。

script.speaker: Tess
script.text: Our exhibition label says the photograph proves that the factory was a pleasant place to work.

script.speaker: Harun
script.text: It shows workers smiling on one occasion, but can a single photograph establish their usual conditions?

script.speaker: Tess
script.text: Perhaps the photographer asked them to pose, although we have no record of that either.

script.speaker: Harun
script.text: Then say what is visible and mention that the circumstances of the photograph are unknown.

script.speaker: Tess
script.text: I will put the wage records nearby so visitors can consider another kind of evidence.

script.speaker: Harun
script.text: Good, as long as we explain their date; conditions may have changed between the records and the photograph.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the original label?

options.text: It draws a broad conclusion from a single image
It claims the photograph was staged without any evidence
It gives wages and working conditions equal importance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 單張照片不足以證明工廠一貫的工作環境。

questions.prompt: How should Tess describe the photograph?

options.text: State that the workers were posed because they are smiling
Use the wage records to date the photograph without checking
State what can be seen and acknowledge unknown circumstances

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 應描述可見內容，並承認拍攝情況不明。

questions.prompt: Why does the date of the wage records matter?

options.text: The date would establish why the workers were smiling
Working conditions might have changed over time
The records must be more recent to be useful at all

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 記錄與照片的時間可能不同，工作環境亦可能已改變。

script.speaker: Luca
script.text: Our design course is assessing the final model, but I spent most of my time testing failed versions.

script.speaker: Fern
script.text: Could the assessor see your development notes as well? They might reveal decisions the model alone cannot show.

script.speaker: Luca
script.text: The instructions allow a short portfolio, though I was going to fill it with photographs of the finished object.

script.speaker: Fern
script.text: Perhaps select a few experiments and explain what each taught you, including one that did not work.

script.speaker: Luca
script.text: I will check the marking criteria so I do not leave out a required technical drawing.

script.speaker: Fern
script.text: That sounds sensible. Showing your process is valuable, provided you still meet the stated requirements.

questions.prompt: Why does Fern suggest including development notes?

options.text: They make the required drawings unnecessary
They establish that the final model performed better than earlier versions
They can show reasoning behind the finished model

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 過程筆記能展示單靠成品看不到的設計決定。

questions.prompt: Why does Luca mention checking the marking criteria?

options.text: He wants to replace the portfolio with a technical drawing alone
He wants to include process evidence without omitting required material
He has decided the experiments matter more than any stated requirement

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Luca 想展示設計過程，同時確保沒有漏交評分準則要求的材料。

questions.prompt: Which principle sums up Fern’s advice?

options.text: Explain selected attempts while satisfying the assessment criteria
Show only the finished object so the assessor is not distracted
Include the full testing record even if required work is omitted

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Fern 建議選擇有意思的實驗解釋，同時符合評核要求。

script.speaker: Mariam
script.text: My uncle wants me to translate his wedding speech, including a joke that depends on two similar-sounding words.

script.speaker: Ed
script.text: A literal translation might preserve the words while losing what makes the joke funny.

script.speaker: Mariam
script.text: I could replace it with a different joke, but then I would be putting my own humour into his speech.

script.speaker: Ed
script.text: Explain the difficulty to him and offer a brief explanation of the wordplay or an alternative he approves.

script.speaker: Mariam
script.text: I will show him both versions. He may prefer a straightforward message if the explanation interrupts the speech.

script.speaker: Ed
script.text: Exactly. Your job is to help his meaning reach the guests, and he should have a say in any substantial change.

questions.prompt: Why might a literal translation fail?

options.text: The guests have already heard an explanation of the joke
The humour relies on sounds that may not work in the other language
The uncle has asked for a completely different speech

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 笑話靠近音字製造效果，直譯未必能在另一種語言保留笑點。

questions.prompt: What does Ed recommend before replacing the joke?

options.text: Discuss the difficulty and seek the uncle’s approval
Choose a new joke and surprise the uncle during the speech
Remove the whole speech to avoid explaining the wordplay

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ed 建議先解釋翻譯難處，重大改動須讓叔叔參與決定。

questions.prompt: Which response would best follow Ed’s advice?

options.text: I will keep every word even if the guests cannot understand the joke.
I will choose whichever version I find funniest without consulting him.
I will ask which version best conveys what he wants to say.

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 應讓叔叔比較版本，選擇最能傳達其心意的一個。

script.speaker: Jo
script.text: The festival committee has asked our dance group to lead the procession, but another group says it has always gone first.

script.speaker: Sanjay
script.text: Have you checked last year’s programme, or are both groups relying on what their members remember?

script.speaker: Jo
script.text: The programmes show that the order has varied. Still, the other group sees going first as recognition of its long involvement.

script.speaker: Sanjay
script.text: Then showing them the programmes may settle the history without addressing why the position matters to them.

script.speaker: Jo
script.text: We could acknowledge their contribution in the introduction and discuss alternating the lead between groups each year.

script.speaker: Sanjay
script.text: That is worth proposing. Agree the arrangement together before printing it, so neither group feels a decision has been imposed.

questions.prompt: Why might the old programmes not resolve the disagreement?

options.text: The position has symbolic importance beyond the historical record
The programmes confirm that the other group always led
Neither group is interested in taking part in the procession

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 另一組重視帶頭位置所代表的肯定，歷年次序並非唯一爭議。

questions.prompt: What compromise does Jo propose?

options.text: Give the other group a permanent right to lead
Keep the order secret until the procession begins
Recognise the group’s contribution and alternate who leads

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Jo 建議公開肯定對方的貢獻，並商量每年輪流帶頭。

questions.prompt: What does Sanjay consider essential?

options.text: The oldest programme should determine every future procession
The groups should agree before the arrangement is published
The committee should print its choice before discussion

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Sanjay 認為應在印製安排前共同議定，避免任何一組覺得被迫接受。

script.speaker: Elise
script.text: At the club dinner the chair traditionally proposes a toast with wine, and this year I have been asked to lead it.

script.speaker: Bilal
script.text: You could keep the words of appreciation while offering a choice of drinks for the toast.

script.speaker: Elise
script.text: Would changing the drink make the older members think I am dismissing the tradition?

script.speaker: Bilal
script.text: You could explain that the shared thanks is the part you want everyone to take part in.

script.speaker: Elise
script.text: I will discuss it with the chair beforehand and make sure the non-alcoholic choices are visible.

script.speaker: Bilal
script.text: That sounds inclusive, and it gives the chair a chance to explain any history you may not know.

questions.prompt: What does Bilal suggest preserving?

options.text: The requirement to use the traditional drink
The custom of asking the chair to lead every toast
The shared expression of appreciation

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Bilal 建議保留共同表達感謝的意義，同時提供不同飲品。

questions.prompt: Why will Elise speak to the chair first?

options.text: To persuade the chair to remove wine from the dinner altogether
To discuss the change and learn any relevant history
To obtain permission to omit the words of thanks

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 事先商量可討論改動，並了解自己未必知道的傳統背景。

questions.prompt: How does Elise feel about changing the toast?

options.text: She worries some members may regard it as disrespectful
She wants to remove the tradition because it excludes younger members
She assumes offering several drinks will weaken the thanks

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Elise 擔心較年長的會員會以為她不尊重傳統。

script.speaker: Poppy
script.text: The high street shops want matching lanterns for the festival, but I found several different designs in the local archive.

script.speaker: Chen
script.text: Then a single design might make the tradition appear more uniform than it really was.

script.speaker: Poppy
script.text: A matching display would be easier to recognise from the bus, though.

script.speaker: Chen
script.text: Could the shops use the same colours but choose different shapes, with a short note explaining the variety?

script.speaker: Poppy
script.text: That would give us a visible theme without suggesting that the archive contains only one pattern.

script.speaker: Chen
script.text: Ask the archive staff to check the note too; we should not invent meanings for shapes we do not understand.

questions.prompt: What tension are they trying to resolve?

options.text: A shared historical explanation versus the need for more shops
A recognisable display versus an accurate account of variety
An attractive display versus a ban on using archive designs

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們要兼顧展示的一致視覺效果與傳統設計的多樣性。

questions.prompt: What compromise does Chen propose?

options.text: Use common colours with varied shapes and an explanation
Copy one archived shape in several unrelated colours
Use several shapes but describe them as one unchanging tradition

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Chen 建議用相同顏色、不同形狀，加上簡短說明。

questions.prompt: Why should archive staff check the note?

options.text: To decide which design should replace all the others
To confirm that the new display exactly reproduces the old festival
To avoid assigning unsupported meanings to the designs

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 檔案館職員可協助避免替不明圖案編造意義。

script.speaker: Molly
script.text: The council wants to close the station footbridge for repairs, leaving the road crossing as the temporary route.

script.speaker: Yusuf
script.text: That crossing is a long detour for people coming from the estate, especially with a pushchair.

script.speaker: Molly
script.text: The engineers say the bridge cannot stay open safely while they replace the supports.

script.speaker: Yusuf
script.text: I am not asking them to keep it open. Could they add a temporary crossing nearer the station?

script.speaker: Molly
script.text: I will raise that at the meeting and ask how long any alternative would take to install.

script.speaker: Yusuf
script.text: Good. The repair and a usable diversion both matter, so residents need the details before work starts.

questions.prompt: What does Yusuf propose?

options.text: Consider a temporary crossing closer to the station
Use the bridge for pushchairs while other people take the diversion
Postpone repairs until residents no longer need the bridge

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Yusuf 建議考慮在車站附近設臨時過路處。

questions.prompt: Why is the existing diversion a concern?

options.text: It prevents anyone from reaching the station at all
It will take engineers too long to repair
It adds a long journey for some residents

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 現有繞道對屋邨居民來說很遠，推嬰兒車尤其不便。

questions.prompt: What is Yusuf’s position on the repair?

options.text: He wants the council to begin work before discussing the diversion
He accepts the closure but wants a practical alternative
He supports the repairs only if the footbridge stays partly open

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他接受因安全需要關橋，但希望有可行的替代路線。

script.speaker: Holly
script.text: Our neighbourhood pharmacy is considering opening later on Fridays, but it would close earlier on Monday to cover staffing.

script.speaker: Idris
script.text: That may help commuters, while making things harder for people who collect prescriptions on Mondays.

script.speaker: Holly
script.text: The owner has asked customers to vote for one option at the counter this week.

script.speaker: Idris
script.text: A counter vote could miss anyone who cannot visit this week. Could she also take responses by phone?

script.speaker: Holly
script.text: I will suggest that, along with recording which times people actually need rather than just their preferred option.

script.speaker: Idris
script.text: The extra detail could reveal whether a smaller change would serve both groups better.

questions.prompt: What is the trade-off in the proposal?

options.text: Friday staff would work longer without any reduction elsewhere
Monday customers would have to collect prescriptions on Friday
Later Friday opening would mean earlier Monday closing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 延長星期五營業時間，代價是星期一提早關門。

questions.prompt: Why suggest telephone responses?

options.text: Telephone responses would replace the need to ask in person
People unable to visit the counter can still contribute
The counter results show that most customers prefer telephone voting

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 電話回覆可讓本星期無法到店的人表達意見。

questions.prompt: What could more detailed feedback reveal?

options.text: Whether a smaller adjustment could help both groups
Whether most customers agree to stop collecting on Mondays
Whether the two groups have the same reason for choosing Friday

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 了解實際需要的時段，或可找出兼顧兩組人的較小改動。

script.speaker: Naveen
script.text: A developer proposes turning the empty office block into flats, with a café on the ground floor.

script.speaker: Claire
script.text: More homes near the railway would be welcome, but the plans show very little space for storing bicycles.

script.speaker: Naveen
script.text: The developer says residents can use the public racks outside the station.

script.speaker: Claire
script.text: Those are often full, and leaving a bike outdoors overnight is different from parking there for an hour.

script.speaker: Naveen
script.text: I will support the conversion in principle but ask the planning committee to address secure storage.

script.speaker: Claire
script.text: That seems reasonable. Supporting more housing does not require accepting every detail of the first plan.

questions.prompt: What concern does Claire raise?

options.text: The development provides more bicycle parking than residents need
The proposed homes lack adequate secure bicycle storage
The conversion would remove the station’s existing bicycle racks

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Claire 認為計劃提供的單車存放空間不足。

questions.prompt: Why are station racks not necessarily a solution?

options.text: They may be full and are less suitable for overnight storage
They are intended for residents rather than rail passengers
They would require the developer to reduce the number of flats

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 車站的單車架經常泊滿，而且在露天過夜存放與短時間停泊的需要不同。

questions.prompt: What is Naveen’s position?

options.text: He supports the plans because public racks meet residents’ needs
He will oppose conversion regardless of any revised storage plan
He supports the conversion subject to resolving a detail

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Naveen 原則上支持改建，但會要求處理單車存放問題。
