script.speaker: Bea
script.text: The village newsletter may go entirely online because printing costs have risen sharply.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: That saves money, but my neighbour uses a basic phone and relies on the paper copy for local news.

script.speaker: Bea
script.text: The editor says subscriptions are too low to pay for printing the current number.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Perhaps fewer copies could be left at the post office and delivered to people who request them.

script.speaker: Bea
script.text: We should ask the volunteers whether a smaller delivery round is manageable before promising it.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Yes, and check whether anyone who needs a copy would be unable to collect one or make a request online.

questions.prompt: Why is an online-only newsletter a problem for some residents?

options.text: They may lack suitable digital access
They would need a subscription even though the website is free
They rely on the paper because it contains different local news

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 部分居民只有基本手機，未必方便網上閱讀。

questions.prompt: What compromise is proposed?

options.text: Keep home delivery but make every copy available only by subscription
Replace delivered copies with collection from the post office alone
Print fewer copies and make them available through collection or delivery

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Martin 建議減少印量，讓居民領取或按需要派送。

questions.prompt: Which question would best help check whether the smaller print run is workable?

options.text: Can we stop consulting volunteers once printing costs fall?
How can someone without internet request a delivered copy?
Which website design would attract the most new advertisers?

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 最後一句關注有需要的人能否領取或申請報紙；追問離線申請方法最切合討論。

script.speaker: Ewan
script.text: The fish smoker has offered to prepare our café’s trout order on Friday, but the delivery van cannot collect it until Monday.

script.speaker: Saira
script.text: Has the producer agreed to store it over the weekend, or does the price assume collection as soon as it is ready?

script.speaker: Ewan
script.text: The quotation only lists the fish and packaging. I had assumed storage was included because the delay is short.

script.speaker: Saira
script.text: We should confirm that rather than treat an unmentioned service as part of the price.

script.speaker: Ewan
script.text: I will ask whether she can hold it until Monday and what that would cost, then compare it with collecting it ourselves on Friday.

script.speaker: Saira
script.text: Include our staff time and transport in that comparison. An option with no storage charge may not be cheaper overall.

questions.prompt: What assumption does Saira question?

options.text: The producer has refused to prepare the order on Friday
The café must buy a different kind of fish
Weekend storage is included in the quoted price

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 報價只列魚及包裝，不能假設已包括週末代存服務。

questions.prompt: What will Ewan confirm with the producer?

options.text: Whether the packaging charge covers the café’s transport
Whether she can store the order and whether there is a charge
Whether Monday collection has already been cancelled

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ewan 會確認能否代存至星期一，以及是否另收費。

questions.prompt: What is Saira’s view of the comparison?

options.text: It should include the café’s time and travel costs
It should be decided by the storage charge alone
It should assume both options require the same amount of work

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Saira 認為應比較整體成本，包括員工時間和交通。

script.speaker: Fran
script.text: The orchard made less cider this year because a late frost damaged some of the apple blossom.

script.speaker: Ollie
script.text: How will the maker divide the limited stock between regular shops and visitors to the farm?

script.speaker: Fran
script.text: Filling the shop orders first would honour our usual arrangements, but it would leave nothing for visitors who come every autumn.

script.speaker: Ollie
script.text: Could the shops agree to smaller allocations, with a clear limit on sales at the farm as well?

script.speaker: Fran
script.text: I will discuss that before confirming quantities. Some shops may already have advertised a tasting event.

script.speaker: Ollie
script.text: Then ask about those commitments rather than assuming every order can be reduced equally. A fair decision needs more than an identical percentage cut.

questions.prompt: What difficulty does the smaller harvest create?

options.text: Visitors have asked for cider from a different grower
There may not be enough stock for both shops and farm visitors
The shops have stopped ordering all orchard products

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 產量減少，可能無法同時滿足店舖訂單及到農場購買的訪客。

questions.prompt: What compromise does Ollie initially suggest?

options.text: Reduce shop allocations and also limit farm sales
Keep every shop order unchanged and close the farm to visitors
Give farm visitors priority over all existing shop orders

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ollie 建議店舖少取一些，同時限制農場現場銷量。

questions.prompt: Why might an identical cut be unfair?

options.text: Every shop has already received exactly the same quantity
Farm visitors have already paid for all the remaining cider
Some shops may have made commitments based on their orders

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 部分店舖可能已按訂量宣傳試飲活動，作決定前須了解其承諾。

script.speaker: Megan
script.text: A visitor wants twenty handwoven scarves in time for the Christmas market, all with the same intricate pattern.

script.speaker: Dev
script.text: Can the weaver produce that many without taking time away from existing commissions?

script.speaker: Megan
script.text: Not at the usual pace. She could simplify the pattern or offer ten scarves by the deadline.

script.speaker: Dev
script.text: The visitor should see a sample of the simpler design before agreeing to it.

script.speaker: Megan
script.text: I will also ask whether the remaining ten could be delivered in January if the original pattern matters most.

script.speaker: Dev
script.text: That gives the buyer a real choice and protects the quality the weaver has promised other customers.

questions.prompt: Why can the weaver not simply accept the order as requested?

options.text: The quantity and deadline conflict with her usual pace and existing work
The original pattern is no longer available to the weaver
The buyer has requested a quantity below the workshop’s minimum

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 按平常製作速度，限期和數量會影響現有訂單。

questions.prompt: Why show a sample of the simpler pattern?

options.text: The sample lets the buyer assume the deadline will no longer matter
The sample proves the original and simpler patterns look identical
The buyer can assess the changed design before agreeing

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 買家可先看簡化後的設計，再決定是否接受。

questions.prompt: What further option will Megan explore?

options.text: Deliver ten simpler scarves and decide the remaining design later
Deliver part of the original design later
Delay all twenty scarves until January without asking the buyer

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Megan 會詢問能否將原設計的部分貨品延至一月交付。

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: At the food fair I want to describe this honey as tasting of heather, but the bees forage over a wide area.

script.speaker: Zaid
script.text: Did the beekeeper test the pollen, or is the description based on the flavour alone?

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: She says it reminds her of heather but has not had the batch analysed.

script.speaker: Zaid
script.text: Then present it as her tasting impression rather than claiming that the honey comes entirely from heather.

script.speaker: Ruth
script.text: I can invite visitors to compare it with another batch and explain why flavours vary by season.

script.speaker: Zaid
script.text: That makes the tasting interesting without suggesting a level of certainty the producer does not have.

questions.prompt: What evidence supports the heather description?

options.text: A pollen analysis confirming a single floral source
Records showing where the bees foraged throughout the season
The beekeeper’s impression of the flavour

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 養蜂人只是根據味道聯想到石南花，並未化驗。

questions.prompt: How should Ruth present the description?

options.text: As a guarantee that every batch will have the same flavour
As a tasting impression rather than a proven sole source
As confirmation that all the bees stayed near heather

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 應說明這是品嚐感受，不可斷言蜜糖完全來自石南花。

questions.prompt: Why compare another batch?

options.text: To explore how flavour can vary without overstating certainty
To prove which flowers supplied all the nectar
To choose one fixed description for every season

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 比較不同批次有助了解季節性味道變化。

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: I remember practising the piano in your hallway, but I thought it belonged to you.

script.speaker: Grandad
script.text: Actually, it belonged to your aunt. She left it with us while her flat was being repaired.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: That explains why it disappeared so suddenly. I had imagined you sold it because I played badly.

script.speaker: Grandad
script.text: Not at all. Your aunt collected it when the builders finished, and you were disappointed for weeks.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: I might ask her whether she remembers the tune I kept trying to learn.

script.speaker: Grandad
script.text: Do. My memory of the dates is uncertain, but I am quite sure the piano was never sold.

questions.prompt: Why did the piano leave the hallway?

options.text: Her aunt sold it when the builders finished
Its owner collected it after repairs to her flat
Grandad gave it away after Nina stopped practising

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 鋼琴原主人在住所維修完成後取回，並非因 Nina 彈得不好而被賣掉。

questions.prompt: What had Nina assumed as a child?

options.text: Her playing caused the piano to be sold
Her aunt had taken it away because she needed lessons
Grandad had borrowed it specifically for Nina’s birthday

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Nina 兒時以為自己彈得不好，令鋼琴被賣掉。

questions.prompt: What distinction does Grandad make about his memory?

options.text: He knows the dates precisely but is unsure whether it was sold
He trusts Nina’s explanation more than his recollection of the owner
He is unsure of the dates but confident it was not sold

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他不肯定日期，但肯定鋼琴沒有被賣掉。

script.speaker: Javed
script.text: I found a photograph of us racing paper boats in the stream behind our old house.

script.speaker: Sister
script.text: I remember that afternoon too, although I thought we had made the boats from newspaper, not coloured paper.

script.speaker: Javed
script.text: The photograph shows coloured sails, but perhaps we added them after the first boats became soggy.

script.speaker: Sister
script.text: That is possible. Mum might remember because she helped us retrieve one that got stuck under a branch.

script.speaker: Javed
script.text: It is funny how the picture brings back the excitement but cannot settle every detail.

script.speaker: Sister
script.text: Yes, and our different memories are worth keeping even if neither of us can reconstruct the whole afternoon.

questions.prompt: What detail do the siblings remember differently?

options.text: The paper used for the boats
Whether they raced in the stream or at the beach
Which parent helped them make the first boat

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們對紙船是否用報紙製作有不同記憶。

questions.prompt: Why might they ask Mum?

options.text: She kept a written record of the paper they used
She can confirm that coloured sails were used from the start
She took part in retrieving a stuck boat

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 媽媽曾幫忙取回卡住的紙船，可能記得當時情況。

questions.prompt: What do they conclude about the photograph?

options.text: It is less useful than memory because it shows only the sails
It prompts memories but does not settle every detail
It settles the material used for every boat that afternoon

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 照片能喚起回憶，卻無法解答所有細節。

title: A voice on an old recording

script.speaker: Ellie
script.text: I found a recording of myself at seven, and my accent sounds different. I thought I had always spoken as I do now.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: We moved towns the following year. You gradually picked up expressions from your new classmates.

script.speaker: Ellie
script.text: I remember copying a few words, but I had assumed I could switch back whenever I wanted.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: You did keep some of the old expressions at home. The change was less sudden than that recording makes it seem.

script.speaker: Ellie
script.text: I will play it to my cousin and ask what she remembers, rather than use one recording to describe my whole childhood.

script.speaker: Dad
script.text: That seems fair. It captures your voice on one occasion, while your cousin may remember how you spoke in different settings.

questions.prompt: What assumption does the recording challenge?

options.text: Ellie moved towns before learning to speak
Ellie’s cousin used the same expressions as her classmates
Ellie’s way of speaking has remained unchanged since childhood

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 錄音中的口音與現在不同，令 Ellie 重新考慮自己說話方式一直沒有改變的想法。

questions.prompt: How does Dad qualify Ellie’s impression of the change?

options.text: It was limited to the words used in that single recording
It happened gradually, with some older expressions retained at home
It happened entirely on the day they moved towns

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 爸爸說轉變是逐漸發生的，而且她在家仍保留一些舊有用語。

questions.prompt: Why does Ellie want her cousin’s recollections?

options.text: They may add information about speech in settings beyond the recording
They can prove that the recording gives a complete account of her speech
They will establish that Ellie deliberately changed her accent overnight

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 親戚的回憶可補充其他場合的說話情況；單次錄音不足以代表整段童年。

script.speaker: Amir
script.text: In this picture I am holding a huge carrot from the school garden, and I always said I grew it myself.

script.speaker: Nana
script.text: You helped water that bed, but the older children planted it before your class joined the project.

script.speaker: Amir
script.text: So calling it my carrot makes the work sound more individual than it was.

script.speaker: Nana
script.text: You were proud because everyone shared the harvest at lunch, not because you wanted the credit alone.

script.speaker: Amir
script.text: I will tell my daughter that part when I show her the photograph.

script.speaker: Nana
script.text: She might enjoy hearing how the garden brought different classes together as much as seeing the carrot.

questions.prompt: What does Nana clarify about the carrot?

options.text: The older children grew it without any help from Amir
Several children contributed to growing it
Amir planted it before the other children joined the project

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 較年長的學生先播種，Amir 也有幫忙澆水。

questions.prompt: Why does Amir reconsider the phrase “my carrot”?

options.text: It overlooks the shared work behind the harvest
It understates his role in planting the whole bed
It makes the harvest sound larger than the photograph suggests

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 說成「我的紅蘿蔔」會忽略其他人的共同付出。

questions.prompt: How does Nana think the photograph could interest Amir’s daughter?

options.text: It could show that Amir contributed more than the older pupils
It could establish that his class planted the garden alone
It could lead to a story about cooperation across classes

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Nana 認為照片可帶出不同班別合作及分享收成的故事。

script.speaker: Nell
script.text: The leisure centre wants to replace disposable cups with reusable ones for its weekend matches.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: That could cut waste, but who will wash and return them between games?

script.speaker: Nell
script.text: The caterer has offered a washing service if the centre provides enough storage for clean cups.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: We should count the cups lost during a trial as well; replacing them often would reduce the benefit.

script.speaker: Nell
script.text: I will propose a four-week trial and compare purchases, washing costs and waste with the current system.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: Include staff time too. A fair comparison needs the less visible work as well as the number of bins emptied.

questions.prompt: What practical issue does Hassan raise first?

options.text: How cups will be washed and returned
How much the centre should charge spectators for the cups
Whether the caterer can supply more disposable cups

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Hassan 首先問杯子如何在比賽之間清洗和歸還。

questions.prompt: Why count lost cups during the trial?

options.text: Lost cups would make the caterer’s storage unnecessary
The number lost would show how well each cup was washed
Frequent replacement could reduce the environmental benefit

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 若經常遺失而須補購，可重用杯的環保效益便會減少。

questions.prompt: What does Hassan imply about counting bins alone?

options.text: It would make a comparison with disposable cups unnecessary
It would miss some of the work and costs involved
It would reveal exactly how many cups had been lost

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 只計垃圾桶數量，會忽略清洗、員工時間等較不顯眼的工作和成本。

script.speaker: Asha
script.text: Dust from the building site has settled on our windowsills, particularly on dry afternoons.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: The contractor says it sprays the ground each morning, but perhaps that is not enough when the wind changes.

script.speaker: Asha
script.text: Should we ask the council to stop the entire project immediately?

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: First, record when the dust is worst and ask the site manager what further controls are possible.

script.speaker: Asha
script.text: I will take dated photographs and invite the neighbours to note their observations separately.

script.speaker: Colin
script.text: That should give the manager useful evidence, although the council may still need to investigate if the problem continues.

questions.prompt: Why might the morning spray be insufficient?

options.text: The contractor sprays only when residents complain
The spray is used indoors rather than on the ground
Conditions can change later in the day

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 風向或日間情況改變，早上灑水未必足夠。

questions.prompt: What will Asha collect?

options.text: Undated photographs of how the windows looked before work started
Dated photographs and neighbours’ separate observations
A joint account that replaces all individual observations

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Asha 會拍下有日期的照片，並請鄰居各自記錄觀察。

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects Colin’s approach?

options.text: Try a documented local response, with council investigation if needed
Insist that the council stop the project before contacting the manager
Accept the morning spraying as sufficient despite further complaints

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Colin 建議先記錄並找地盤經理處理；若問題持續，議會仍可能需要調查。

script.speaker: Liam
script.text: I have a ceramic bowl with a sharp broken edge and was about to put it in the glass recycling bank.

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: The council guidance separates ceramics from glass because they melt differently during recycling.

script.speaker: Liam
script.text: Could a charity shop use it for a mosaic, or would donating a sharp broken bowl create a problem?

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: Ask a local craft group first and describe the damage; do not leave it at a shop without checking.

script.speaker: Liam
script.text: If nobody can use it, I will wrap the sharp edges and follow the council’s disposal instructions.

script.speaker: Farah
script.text: That avoids contaminating the glass collection while still giving the bowl a chance of being reused safely.

questions.prompt: Why should the bowl stay out of glass recycling?

options.text: The council requires every damaged household object to be reused
Ceramics behave differently from glass during processing
Ceramics are accepted only when they are unbroken

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 陶瓷與玻璃在回收處理時的熔化方式不同。

questions.prompt: What does Farah recommend before offering the bowl?

options.text: Ask a craft group and explain its condition
Leave it at the shop with a note instead of asking
Offer it to a group without mentioning the damage

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Farah 建議先詢問手工藝團體，並說明碗的破損情況。

questions.prompt: What is Liam’s fallback?

options.text: Use the glass bank once the sharp edges are wrapped
Leave it beside the recycling bank for someone else to use
Wrap sharp edges and follow local disposal guidance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 若無人可用，他會包好銳利邊緣並按議會指引棄置。

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: Several coaches wait outside the school with their engines running before the afternoon trip.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: The drivers may be keeping the heating on, but the exhaust gathers near the entrance.

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: Could we ask the school to move the waiting point away from the doors?

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: That might help at the entrance but move the exhaust towards nearby houses. We should consider both.

script.speaker: Mira
script.text: I will ask the coach company when engines need to run and whether drivers can switch them off while waiting.

script.speaker: Paul
script.text: Then the school can choose an arrangement based on the actual constraints rather than simply shifting the problem.

questions.prompt: What concern does Paul raise about moving the coaches?

options.text: The exhaust could affect nearby homes instead
The coaches would no longer be able to use heating
The new waiting point would necessarily make journeys longer

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Paul 擔心搬遷等候地點只會把廢氣轉移到附近住宅。

questions.prompt: What will Mira ask the coach company?

options.text: Whether moving the coaches would make the trip cheaper
Whether the drivers could leave before pupils are ready
When engines are necessary and whether they can be switched off

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Mira 會詢問引擎何時必須運轉，以及等候時能否熄匙。

questions.prompt: What principle guides their approach?

options.text: Ask the company to keep heating on without checking alternatives
Investigate constraints and effects before choosing a solution
Choose a waiting point according to distance from the school alone

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 他們希望先了解限制及對不同地點的影響，再選擇方案。

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: The library wants to run a public speaking competition with a prize for the best argument.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: How will the judges distinguish a strong argument from a confident performance?

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: They could assess the evidence and reasoning separately from delivery, with the criteria available before entry.

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: That would help. I would also give everyone the same preparation time rather than reward those who can improvise quickly.

script.speaker: Zara
script.text: Should we let judges question each speaker afterwards to see whether they understand their evidence?

script.speaker: Theo
script.text: Yes, provided the questions are comparable in difficulty. A challenging follow-up for one person and a simple factual check for another would undermine fairness.

questions.prompt: What concern does Theo raise first?

options.text: The prize may attract too many experienced judges
Speakers may all choose exactly the same evidence
Confidence could be mistaken for the quality of an argument

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Theo 擔心評審把自信的表現誤當成論證有力。

questions.prompt: How would Zara make the judging clearer?

options.text: Award the prize to whoever answers most quickly
Publish separate criteria for reasoning and delivery
Let each judge decide privately what counts as a good argument

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Zara 建議預先公布準則，把論證及表達分開評分。

questions.prompt: What condition does Theo place on follow-up questions?

options.text: They should offer a comparable level of challenge
They should be identical even when the topics differ
They should be harder for less confident speakers

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Theo 認為追問難度須相若，才不會令參賽者受到不公平對待。

script.speaker: Ellen
script.text: Some firms have trialled a four-day working week, and I wonder whether every workplace should adopt one.

script.speaker: Musa
script.text: It could improve work-life balance, but a hospital cannot simply close its wards for an extra day.

script.speaker: Ellen
script.text: Staff could work different days, although the employer might need more people to maintain coverage.

script.speaker: Musa
script.text: Exactly. We need to know whether staff would work fewer hours or simply fit the same hours into longer days, and how services would be covered.

script.speaker: Ellen
script.text: I would compare staff wellbeing and service quality during a trial, rather than measuring only costs.

script.speaker: Musa
script.text: And ask workers whether they are fitting the same workload into less time, since that could increase pressure.

questions.prompt: Why does Musa mention a hospital?

options.text: Hospital staff already have fewer working hours than other staff
Some services need coverage throughout the week
A shorter week necessarily means a service closes for an extra day

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 醫院服務須持續運作，不能因縮短工作週便額外關閉一天。

questions.prompt: What would Ellen assess during a trial?

options.text: Staff wellbeing and service quality as well as costs
The cost savings alone before considering staff experience
Whether staff can complete all their work without changing the rota

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Ellen 會評估員工福祉、服務質素和成本。

questions.prompt: What risk does Musa identify?

options.text: Maintaining coverage always means staff must work longer hours
Different working days prevent staff from coordinating their work
The same workload compressed into fewer hours may increase pressure

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 若工作量不變但集中在較少時間完成，壓力可能增加。

title: Inviting an expert to the panel

script.speaker: Freya
script.text: Our residents’ panel is considering flood prevention, and I want to invite the engineer who designed the proposed scheme.

script.speaker: Adeel
script.text: Her expertise would be useful, though she also has an interest in the proposal being accepted.

script.speaker: Freya
script.text: Would that mean she should not be allowed to speak at all?

script.speaker: Adeel
script.text: I would hear her explanation and declare her connection to the scheme, then invite someone independent to assess the assumptions.

script.speaker: Freya
script.text: We should circulate the technical summary beforehand so residents can prepare questions instead of just hearing competing opinions.

script.speaker: Adeel
script.text: Agreed. Being open about someone’s role helps the audience evaluate a contribution; it does not make the contribution worthless.

questions.prompt: Why does Adeel suggest an independent assessment?

options.text: The designer has expertise but also an interest in the outcome
The designer has no relevant knowledge of the scheme
The panel has already rejected every technical explanation

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 設計者雖有專業知識，但亦與方案能否獲接納有利益關係。

questions.prompt: Why circulate the technical summary in advance?

options.text: Residents can avoid hearing the engineer’s explanation
The independent expert can make the final decision alone
Residents can prepare informed questions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 預先發放技術摘要，能讓居民有資料作基礎準備問題。

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects Adeel’s position?

options.text: Technical expertise removes the need to disclose an interest
A declared connection should inform how evidence is assessed
A connection to a proposal makes every statement unreliable

questions.explanation_zh_hk: Adeel 認為公開交代關係有助評估發言，並不代表內容全無價值。

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: You said village life is less stressful than city life. Does that apply to everyone?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: No, I should qualify that. It may be quieter for some people, but isolation or limited transport can create stress.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: Can you give an example of the transport problem?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: Someone working shifts might depend on a car if the last bus leaves before their workplace closes.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: So are you saying that cities always offer a better quality of life?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: Not always. My point is that the advantages depend on a person’s circumstances and the services available.

questions.prompt: How does the candidate revise the original claim?

options.text: Village life is less stressful whenever transport is available
City life is quieter for everyone who works shifts
Village life may be quieter, but it can bring other pressures

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 候選人承認鄉村可能較寧靜，但也有交通和孤立等壓力。

questions.prompt: What example supports the revised view?

options.text: A shift worker might find every city journey more stressful
A shift worker may lack a suitable bus
A shift worker might need a car despite having a suitable late bus

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 輪班人士下班後可能沒有巴士可乘，因而需要依賴私家車。

questions.prompt: What is the best summary of the final answer?

options.text: Quality of life depends on personal circumstances and services
Village residents benefit from quiet surroundings regardless of their needs
The quality of transport is the only factor in choosing where to live

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 生活質素取決於個人情況和可使用的服務，不能一概而論。

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: Your college proposes making all student feedback anonymous. Would you support that?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: It could help students raise concerns honestly, provided the feedback still gives teachers enough detail to act on.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: What if a comment simply says that a lesson was bad?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: I would ask the form to prompt for an example and a suggested improvement, without requiring the student’s name.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: Would teachers then be expected to accept every suggestion?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: No. They should explain what can change and why some requests cannot be met. Being heard is different from having every preference adopted.

questions.prompt: What condition does the candidate attach to anonymity?

options.text: Teachers must act on every suggestion they receive
Comments should still contain useful detail
Every comment must identify the student’s classmate

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 考生認為匿名意見仍須有足夠細節，教師才可跟進。

questions.prompt: How does the candidate address a vague negative comment?

options.text: Use prompts that ask for an example and an improvement
Remove anonymity so the teacher can challenge the student
Exclude all negative comments from the feedback form

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 考生建議表格提示學生提供例子及改善建議，同時保留匿名。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the final answer make?

options.text: Anonymous feedback is less honest than named feedback
A teacher’s explanation makes student feedback unnecessary
Listening to feedback does not mean implementing every request

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 聆聽意見不等於接受每項要求，教師應交代能否改動及原因。

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: You suggest that every college student should study another language. Would that suit everyone?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: I think it has value, but a compulsory advanced course could be unrealistic for students with different starting points.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: Suppose the college offers a short introductory course instead. Would that meet your aim?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: It could encourage students to try a language, although a few sessions would not make them fluent.

script.speaker: Examiner
script.text: How would you judge whether the course had succeeded?

script.speaker: Candidate
script.text: I would look at whether students could handle a simple exchange and wanted to continue, rather than compare them with advanced speakers.

questions.prompt: How does the candidate qualify the original proposal?

options.text: The level and starting points need consideration
Every student should take the same advanced course
Language learning has no value outside specialist courses

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 考生認為學習語言有價值，但須考慮學生起點及課程程度。

questions.prompt: What limitation of an introductory course does the candidate recognise?

options.text: It prevents students from studying the language further
It would require all students to be advanced already
It cannot produce fluency in just a few sessions

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 短期入門課可鼓勵嘗試，但幾堂課不足以令人說得流利。

questions.prompt: Which result would meet the candidate’s suggested measure of success?

options.text: Beginners memorise advanced grammar without using the language
Beginners manage a basic exchange and show interest in continuing
Beginners match the fluency of students with years of study

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 考生的準則是初學者能作簡單交流，並有意繼續學習。

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: I booked two seats for Saturday, but your email says the performance has moved to Sunday afternoon.

script.speaker: Box office
script.text: That is correct. Saturday’s performance was cancelled after a technical fault, and we offered Sunday as an alternative.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: I cannot attend then. Does the email mean I have already accepted the new date?

script.speaker: Box office
script.text: No. You do not have to accept Sunday; you can request a refund or choose another available performance.

script.speaker: Visitor
script.text: Please refund both seats. I paid by card, so will it go back to the same account?

script.speaker: Box office
script.text: Yes, the refund should reach the same account within ten working days. I will send confirmation now; please contact us if the money has not arrived after that.

questions.prompt: What has the visitor misunderstood about Sunday’s performance?

options.text: They think Saturday’s technical fault also cancelled Sunday
They think Sunday seats cost more than the original booking
They think an offered alternative may already count as acceptance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 訪客誤以為收到替代場次通知，就可能代表自己已接受改期。

questions.prompt: What does the visitor choose?

options.text: Keep the booking until another Saturday is available
A refund for both seats
Accept Sunday while requesting a partial refund

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 訪客無法在星期日出席，因此要求退回兩張票的款項。

questions.prompt: What should the visitor do if the refund has not arrived after ten working days?

options.text: Contact the box office
Treat the cancellation email as proof that the refund has arrived
Choose another performance before contacting the box office

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 退款一般十個工作天內退回原付款帳戶；若未收到，應聯絡售票處。

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: The allotment watering rota has changed because the tap near the gate is being repaired on Thursday.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I am down for Thursday morning. Should I still come at nine?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Yes, but use the tap beside the shed and water the seed beds first; the established plants can wait until Friday.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I usually collect the key from the café. Will it be there as normal?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Not this week. The café opens late, so collect the key from the library, which opens at eight. Please return it there before noon.

script.speaker: Volunteer
script.text: I will collect it there before nine, water the seed beds using the shed tap, and return it to the library before noon.

questions.prompt: Why has the rota changed?

options.text: The seed beds no longer require watering
The tap near the gate needs repair
The shed tap is being repaired on Friday

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 入口附近的水龍頭星期四要維修，因此澆水安排有變。

questions.prompt: What does the revised watering instruction imply?

options.text: The seed beds are more urgent than the established plants
The established plants must be watered before Thursday
The gate tap should be used briefly before the repairs begin

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 協調員安排先澆育苗床，已長成的植物可等至星期五，表示育苗床較急需澆水。

questions.prompt: Where will the volunteer collect and return the key?

options.text: Collect at the café and return to the library
Collect at the library and return to the shed
At the library

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 本星期須到八時開門的圖書館取鎖匙，並在中午前交回同一地點。

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: The course page says the field trip costs thirty pounds, but your announcement mentioned twenty-five.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: The page is out of date. The trip costs twenty-five pounds, including the coach but not lunch.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Can I pay on the morning of the trip, or is there an earlier deadline?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Please pay by next Wednesday so we can confirm the coach booking. A free packed lunch can be requested separately.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: I will submit the payment tomorrow and request the lunch today. Is the departure still at eight?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: It is now eight thirty from the college entrance. I will update the page and send the corrected details to everyone.

questions.prompt: What does the corrected trip price include?

options.text: The coach journey
A packed lunch automatically supplied to everyone
The coach journey and a compulsory lunch charge

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 更正後的二十五鎊費用包括旅遊巴，但不包括午膳。

questions.prompt: Why does the student need to take two separate actions?

options.text: The coach and lunch must both be paid for separately
The departure time will change only after payment and a lunch request
The trip payment and the optional packed-lunch request are separate

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 旅費包括旅遊巴，但午餐須另行申請；免費午餐不會自動提供。

questions.prompt: What is the revised departure arrangement?

options.text: Eight thirty from the coach station
Eight thirty from the college entrance
Eight from the college entrance

questions.explanation_zh_hk: 出發時間改為八時三十分，地點是學院入口。
